findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring the write lock causes duplicate manifest loads
findings.body: After reading the cache under RLock and releasing it, the function takes the write lock at line 48 but never re-checks whether the cache was filled by another goroutine in the meantime. On a cold start (or any time the cache is nil in non-Dev env), N concurrent callers all observe `ret == nil` at line 45 and then queue on the write lock; each one runs the full read path (lines 51-67, including reading and JSON-decoding assets-manifest.json, and its error paths) and overwrites the cache. The final value is still correct, but N concurrent requests produce N serialized disk reads/parses instead of one, and every queued request is blocked for the whole duration of the I/O. This is the classic double-checked-locking omission: re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` and return the cached value early.

findings.title: No test exercises concurrent GetWebAssets calls
findings.body: The PR's sole purpose is to eliminate a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache, but it adds no test. A race like this is only reliably caught by running concurrent GetWebAssets invocations under `go test -race`; without such a test, a future refactor could reintroduce an unguarded read/write without CI noticing. Add a test that spawns multiple goroutines calling GetWebAssets against a temp manifest and asserts they all get a non-nil, consistent result (run with -race).
